approach: Fix it where it starts: the driver. `output_from_result` in claude.rs recognises a usage-limit reply (an error result with no model usage whose text has 'limit' and 'resets'). It returns a new `InvocationOutcome::Limited` output with zero cost, unmeasured zero tokens and a detail that leads with the parsed reset time. Unmeasured tokens mean the gate's 'measured tokens but no usage for the requested model' rule does not fire. The run pipeline closes a job whose planner, producer or verifier call returned Limited as `Failed` with a retryable environment reason, the same path the low-disk-before-verifier case uses, so the candidate and resume mark are kept and `athena retry` resumes. Drain recognises that reason in `run_job` and ends the item with a new `Stop::UsageLimit` before `failures` is incremented. `athena status` shows the hold from a pure function over the invocation records and an injected `now`. This revision drops fake.rs and docs/records.md from the plan; the remaining files outside the brief's list are each necessary (see decisions).

decisions.choice: Add `InvocationOutcome::Limited` (snake_case `limited`) in crates/athena-data/src/records.rs and extend its round-trip test. This file is outside the brief's list but necessary.
decisions.reason: The request says 'record the invocation as limited', and the reading's assumptions anticipate a 'limited' state. The enum is defined only in records.rs, so no listed file can add the variant. The variant lets status, run and tests tell a limit from an error without parsing text. Uses elsewhere are `==` or `matches!`, so nothing else breaks (grep of InvocationOutcome:: found no exhaustive match outside tests).

rejected.option: Keep outcome Error and mark the limit only by a detail prefix
rejected.why: Every consumer would parse text to tell a limit from a failure, and the brief asks for a limited record.

rejected.option: Add a reset-time field to Invocation
rejected.why: A schema change; the record denies unknown fields. The reset time fits in the detail.

decisions.choice: The limited output has `usage_measured: false`, zero usage, empty `models_used` and `cost_usd: Some(0.0)`. The detail is 'usage limit (resets at <RFC3339>): <reply text, 200 chars max>', with the reset time first so truncation cannot cut it.
decisions.reason: `check_invocation` in crates/athena-gate/src/reconcile.rs checks token reconciliation only when all four quantities are Measured, and `invocation_record` (crates/athena-core/src/invocation.rs line 175) turns `usage_measured: false` into lower-bound tokens. A reported zero cost passes the cost rule, which is skipped when `models_used` is empty. The gate is unchanged, as the brief requires.

rejected.option: Insert a zero ModelUsage entry for the requested model
rejected.why: It shows a model as used when no call ran.

rejected.option: Relax the gate for error records
rejected.why: Out of scope: the brief forbids changing the gate's rules for other records.

decisions.choice: Close a limited job as `Failed` with a reason starting `environment: usage limit`. A `USAGE_LIMIT` constant lives in run/mod.rs, and `disk::is_environment_reason` (crates/athena-core/src/disk.rs, outside the brief's list but necessary) also accepts it. A helper `usage_limit_of(reason)` returns the reset text.
decisions.reason: `resumable_stop` in disk.rs (line 221) decides what `athena retry` may resume, and it accepts a Failed job only if `is_environment_reason` holds, which tests only the LOW_DISK prefix. Without a disk.rs edit the kept candidate could not be retried. The reason also keeps the resume mark and reads as not a work failure to the scope guard (run/mod.rs line 544).

rejected.why: It ripples through the outcome schema, retry rules and docs.
It would look interrupted and be re-read without a reason.

decisions.choice: Drain finds the limit in `run_job` with `athena_core::run::usage_limit_of(&run.reason)` when the run failed, so the `Run` struct and every `Run` constructor stay unchanged. It adds `RunStep::UsageLimit`, `ItemEnd::UsageLimit` and `Stop::UsageLimit` (label 'usage limit'). `work()` returns before `failures += 1`, and `finish` sets the stop with the reset text. `Report` gains `usage_limit: Option<String>`.
decisions.reason: A limit needs its own stop reason and must not touch the failure count; every later model call would fail alike, so drain stops at once. Reading the reason keeps the drain test free of a hand-set flag: the stub returns only the reason string the run pipeline writes, and a run test pins that string.

rejected.option: Add a `usage_limit` field to `Run`, set in `RealSteps::run`
rejected.why: More constructors to change, and the stub test would then set the flag by hand, so the mapping from reason to stop would go untested.

rejected.option: Count it as a failure but relabel the stop
rejected.why: The brief says the failure counter stays unchanged.
Out of scope: no automatic waiting.

decisions.choice: `crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs` is touched (outside the brief's list but necessary): the drain 'stopped' line and the `athena status` text are both rendered only in `display::drain` and `display::status`. main.rs only prints them and holds the help text.
decisions.reason: The brief requires the stop reason to name the reset time and `athena status` to show the limit; neither can be printed without editing the renderer. The edit is one match arm in `drain` and one conditional line in `status`.

rejected.option: Print the extra lines from main.rs
rejected.why: The drain report would show a generic 'usage limit' line first and a second line elsewhere; the status JSON and text paths would diverge.

decisions.choice: `athena status` computes the hold with a pure `usage_limit_hold(records, now)` in status.rs; `status()` calls it with `crate::now()`. The hold exists when the newest Limited invocation's reset time (parsed from its detail by `reset_time_in`) is after `now` and no later invocation succeeded. Reset text that does not parse falls back to one hour from the record's end time.
decisions.reason: An injected `now` lets a test show the hold, then none after the reset, with no clock sleeping. No new data file is added.

rejected.option: A marker file in the state dir
rejected.why: Adds a data file and can go stale.

decisions.choice: Do not change crates/athena-agent/src/fake.rs or docs/records.md. In the run test, a test-local driver wraps `FakeAgentDriver`; for the verifier role it feeds the limit line through `StreamState::on_line` and the real `output_from_result`.
decisions.reason: fake.rs is outside the brief's list. The test-local wrapper reaches the same record shape with the real recogniser, and it follows the pattern of `record_from` in crates/athena-core/src/invocation.rs tests (StreamState → output_from_result → invocation_record → check_invocation). The `Limited` variant is described by its doc comment and the CHANGELOG entry; docs/records.md has no test tied to the outcome list, so skipping it is safe.

rejected.option: Teach FakeAgentDriver to build unmeasured Limited turns
rejected.why: Widens scope, and the double would hand-build the shape the real driver is meant to produce.
Outside the listed files; raised as an open question for a follow-up.

decisions.choice: Parse the reset in claude.rs from 'resets <Mon> <day>, <h>(am|pm) (UTC)', and take the year from the invocation's end time, rolling to next year if that date is already past. The helper `reset_time_in(detail)` is public so status.rs reuses it.
decisions.reason: The reply has no year. Other limit kinds share the 'limit'/'resets' wording, so the kind is matched loosely.

rejected.option: Treat an unparseable reply as an ordinary error
rejected.why: The job would fail as before.

files.purpose: Recogniser for the limit reply, reset-time parser (`reset_time_in`, public), Limited zero-cost unmeasured output from `output_from_result`, `MODE=limit` stand-in branch, tests for criteria 1 and 5.
Add `InvocationOutcome::Limited` with a doc comment, and extend the existing outcome round-trip test. Necessary for 'recorded as limited'; outside the brief's list.
`is_environment_reason` also accepts the usage-limit prefix so `resumable_stop` lets `athena retry` resume the kept candidate. One condition and a test line. Outside the brief's list but necessary.

`USAGE_LIMIT` constant, reason builder and `usage_limit_of(reason)`; close planner, producer and verifier Limited outputs as an environment failure; run tests for criteria 2 and 5 with the test-local `LimitedVerifier`.

The drain 'stopped' line names the reset time for the usage-limit stop, and `status` prints a 'usage limit' line while the hold lasts; render tests. Both texts are rendered only here. Outside the brief's list but necessary.
Add a 'usage limit' entry to the drain help's 'Stop reasons' list.
`UsageLimitView`, `StatusView.usage_limit` (skipped in JSON when None), pure `usage_limit_hold(records, now)`, `status()` wiring with `crate::now()`, tests.
Unreleased entry for the usage-limit handling, the 'usage limit' stop reason and the status display.

steps: Read the sites to change: the `AgentDriver` trait, `athena_with`, `counting`, `Counts` and the retry call in `low_disk_before_the_verifier_resumes_without_planner_or_producer` in run/mod.rs; the `Stub` and `limits` helpers and the `Stop` label/meaning/ALL code in drain.rs; and the Report constructor near drain.rs line 1417. Add `ItemEnd::UsageLimit`, make `work()` return it before `failures += 1`, and have `finish` call `set_stop(Stop::UsageLimit, ..)` carrying the reset text. Add `Stop::UsageLimit` (label 'usage limit', meaning, `ALL`) and `Report.usage_limit`. Add `LimitedStub` and the criterion 3 test.

Run `cargo fmt --all`, then `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`. Fix failures, including the budgets and help-text tests.

risks.risk: The matcher is too loose and turns an ordinary error, or a success quoting the words, into a limit.
risks.mitigation: It requires is_error true, no usage for the requested model, and both 'limit' and 'resets' wording. Criterion 5 tests cover the near misses.

risks.risk: A new `InvocationOutcome` variant breaks record parsing, a validation list, or a match elsewhere.
risks.mitigation: A grep found only `==` and `matches!` uses outside tests. The records round-trip test is extended and the full `cargo test --locked` is criterion 7.

risks.risk: The job-totals check (`check_outcome`) rejects a closing outcome whose invocations include an unmeasured zero record.
risks.mitigation: `go` in the criterion 2 test closes the job through the normal commit path, so a totals violation would fail the test. If `sums` mishandles lower-bound zeros, report it rather than change the gate.

risks.risk: The reset year or zone is guessed wrong, so the hold lasts too long or ends early.
risks.mitigation: The year comes from the invocation's end time with a next-year roll. Unparseable text gives a bounded one-hour fallback. Tests pin 'Oct 29, 6pm (UTC)' to 2026-10-29T18:00:00Z.

risks.risk: Scope: records.rs, disk.rs and display.rs are outside the brief's list.
risks.mitigation: Each is necessary and the edit is minimal (one variant, one condition, two render arms); fake.rs and docs/records.md were dropped from the plan.

risks.risk: After the reset, the next drain hits the limit again if the reset was misread.
risks.mitigation: The call is rejected in about 2 s at no cost, and drain stops at once with the same reason and no failure counted.

demonstrations.method: Unit and driver-process tests in claude.rs. (a) Feed the result line (is_error true, text "You've hit your weekly limit · resets Oct 29, 6pm (UTC)", zero usage, empty modelUsage) to `StreamState::on_line`, then call the production function `output_from_result` and assert the output. (b) Add a `MODE=limit` branch to the existing `STAND_IN` shell script, placed before its assistant echo, and run it through `ClaudeCodeDriver::invoke` with the existing `stand_in`, `driver` and `spec` helpers. (c) A third case parses 'session limit · resets 3pm (UTC)'. The stand-in and helpers exist today (claude.rs lines 585 to 646); step 2 adds the branch and tests.
demonstrations.observes: Outcome is Limited; the detail contains 'resets at 2026-10-29T18:00:00Z' and the reply text; `cost_usd` is Some(0.0); usage is zero; `usage_measured` is false; `models_used` is empty. This holds through both the pure function and the real driver process path, and a session-kind reply is also recognised.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the recogniser, `output_from_result` returns outcome Error with `usage_measured` true, so the outcome, detail and measured assertions fail.

demonstrations.method: Run test in crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs, patterned on `low_disk_before_the_verifier_resumes_without_planner_or_producer`. Build the Athena with the existing `athena_with(.., PASSES, .., counting(..))`, then replace its `driver` field (an `Arc<dyn AgentDriver>` the harness already builds) with a test-local `LimitedVerifier`. That wrapper holds an inner `FakeAgentDriver` made with the same `counting` script and registry and delegates every role but the verifier. For the verifier it passes the limit line through `StreamState::on_line` and the real `output_from_result` and returns that output, so no recognition logic is in the double. Entry points: `Athena::go`, then `Athena::retry` with the plain driver restored. The `LimitedVerifier` wrapper is added in step 5; the `Athena.driver` field and the harness exist today. Confirm the `AgentDriver` trait's method set in step 1.
demonstrations.observes: (1) `go` returns Failed with a reason starting 'environment: usage limit', `is_environment_reason` is true, and `usage_limit_of(&reason)` returns the reset time (and None for a low-disk reason). (2) The stored invocation record has outcome Limited and cost 0, and `athena_gate::reconcile::check_invocation(path, &record)` returns no violations, called on the stored record. (3) The resume mark exists and the candidate fingerprint is recorded. (4) With the plain driver, `retry` resumes, the job passes, and the planner and producer counters stay at (0, 1, 0). (5) A control run with an Error verifier turn closes without the usage-limit reason. The drain half of 'no failure counted' is criterion 3.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the Limited handling, the verifier branch sets `verifier_failure`, the job closes Rejected, the resume mark is removed, and the state, reason and resume assertions fail. If the output were measured, `check_invocation` would return the 'measured tokens, but no usage for the requested model' violation.

Its `run` logs the call and returns `Run { outcome: Some(OutcomeState::Failed), reason: <the reason string the run pipeline writes, built with the same builder run/mod.rs exports>, .. }`. Call `drain_with` (line 1303) with the existing `limits()` and `Quiet` ui. The new stub, `RunStep::UsageLimit`, `ItemEnd::UsageLimit` and `Stop::UsageLimit` are added in step 7.
demonstrations.observes: `report.stop == Stop::UsageLimit` and its label is 'usage limit'; `report.usage_limit` contains the reset time; `report.failed_item` is None; `run` was called once (so `failures` was never incremented and no retry was tried); the second item never started; the job line outcome reads 'usage limit'; `display::drain(&report)` contains 'usage limit' and the reset time and does not contain 'repeated failure'. The existing `Stop::ALL` loops (drain.rs line 2348 and crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs line 1279) now cover the new variant.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the new branch, the failed Run falls into the 'other' arm of `run_job`, is retried, and the stop becomes RepeatedFailure; the stop and call-count assertions fail.

demonstrations.method: Two tests. In status.rs tests, build `Records` with the existing `invocation(job, seq, role, usd)` helper (line 1615), set outcome Limited and the detail 'usage limit (resets at 2026-10-29T18:00:00Z): …', and call the production function `usage_limit_hold(&records, now)` with a `now` before the reset, one after it, and one before it with a later Success invocation present. In display.rs tests (added there if no test module exists), render `display::status` on a `StatusView` with `usage_limit` set and one with it None. `usage_limit_hold`, the field and the render line are added in steps 6 and 8.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core usage_limit_hold && cargo test -p athena-cli status_usage_limit
demonstrations.observes: The hold carries the limit text and reset time while `now` is before the reset. It is None once `now` is past the reset, and None when a later invocation succeeded. The rendered status contains 'usage limit' and the reset time only in the holding case, and neither when None.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the hold function and field, the tests do not compile; with a hold that ignored `now`, the after-reset case would still show the limit and fail.

demonstrations.method: claude.rs tests: a result with is_error true, subtype 'error_during_execution' and text 'API Error: 500', and one with is_error true and text 'rate limit exceeded' with no 'resets' wording, each give outcome Error with the detail unchanged from today. A successful result with usage that quotes 'hit your limit … resets' gives Success. The run/mod.rs control (Error verifier turn) closes without the usage-limit reason. Existing drain tests with a plain Failed Run (no usage-limit reason) still stop as RepeatedFailure after two attempts.
demonstrations.observes: Ordinary errors keep the Error outcome and measured tokens, closing reasons and drain failure counting are unchanged, and a drain with a plain failed `Run` still stops as 'repeated failure'.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the matcher were too loose (any error, or a success quoting the words), these cases would show Limited or a changed outcome, and the failure-count tests would fail.

demonstrations.method: Add an Unreleased entry to CHANGELOG.md naming the cause (a weekly limit reply recorded as an error and counted as a failure twice), the Limited invocation outcome, the retryable job, the 'usage limit' stop reason with the reset time, and the `athena status` line.
demonstrations.observes: The entry sits under Unreleased and mentions the stop reason and the status display.
demonstrations.fails_without: With no entry, grep finds no 'usage limit' line in the Unreleased section.

demonstrations.method: Run the three checks Athena runs on the final tree, which includes the new tests from criteria 1 to 5, the extended records round-trip test, the budgets test (`system_facts_budgets_match_computed`) and the help/`Stop::ALL` tests.

demonstrations.fails_without: fmt fails on unformatted new code; clippy fails on an unused import or dead variant; the tests fail if `Limited` is missing from the records round-trip, if `Stop::UsageLimit` is missing from `Stop::ALL` or the drain help list in main.rs, or if any of the new behavior tests of criteria 1 to 5 fails.

The recogniser keys on is_error plus no model usage for the requested model plus the 'limit' and 'resets' wording; the incident record (2 s, no usage) is the only evidence. A captured line would confirm it.

Reader, steward, auditor, audience, introspection and pin calls check `outcome != Success` and are outside the listed files. A limit hit there is recorded as Limited, which the gate accepts, but it surfaces as that stage's own error, not as a drain hold. Should a follow-up cover them?
